text:
Micah: Hi all — first week here! Trying to get my MacBook Air M2 dev env working. Followed the quickstart but `asdf` isn't picking up rust and node. Also my ssh keys won't load into the agent. Anyone have a checklist?
Tara: welcome Micah! :wave: quick checklist—did you install Xcode CLT and Homebrew for arm64? run `xcode-select --install` then `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"`
Micah: yep CLT installed. Brew is at /opt/homebrew. I installed asdf via brew and added the lines to my `~/.zshrc` like the guide said.
Devon: two common traps: 1) on apple silicon, ensure `brew` is in your PATH early (put `/opt/homebrew/bin` in `~/.zprofile`), 2) if you're using `direnv`/`.envrc` or `fish` the shell init lines differ.
Micah: my shell is zsh (default). I put `source /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh` in `.zshrc`. Still `asdf list all rust` errors with "command not found".
Tara: try adding `eval "$(asdf init -)"` instead of sourcing the script directly. Also restart the terminal or `exec $SHELL`.
Micah: ok did that. Now `asdf plugin-add rust https://github.com/codebergorg/asdf-rust.git` fails with SSL error. Curl works though.
Kenji: sometimes the plugin URL changed — use `asdf plugin-add rust rust-lang --git` (the org name differs by plugin). Example commands:

```
asdf plugin-add rust https://github.com/rust-lang/asdf-rust.git
asdf install rust latest
asdf global rust latest
```

Kenji: if you still get SSL, run `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=1 git clone ...` as a debug step but don't keep that setting.
Micah: thanks kenji, plugin add worked after using the rust-lang repo. Installed rust fine. Node is weird: yarn says node v18 but `node -v` shows v20. My app wants v18.
Devon: check `~/.tool-versions` — asdf sets versions there. Also verify your shell is loading asdf before NVM or system node. `which node` and `which asdf` help.
Micah: `.tool-versions` had nodejs 18.15.0 but `which node` points to `/usr/local/bin/node` — looks like an old intel brew install.
Tara: remove the intel brew path or reorder PATH to prefer `/opt/homebrew/bin`. You can find duplicates with `ls -l $(which node)` and `brew --prefix`.
Micah: fixed PATH in `.zprofile`, restarted terminal — node now v18 via asdf. SSH agent still failing: `ssh-add -l` says "Could not open a connection to your authentication agent." I use Keychain and git prompts keep asking for passphrase.
Kenji: on macs, the Apple SSH agent integration can be weird with asdf/env setups. If you use `ssh-agent` manually, do `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` then `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to store in keychain. For newer macOS, `-K` is deprecated — use `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain` or add `AddKeysToAgent yes` and `UseKeychain yes` in `~/.ssh/config`:

```
Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

Devon: also watch direnv: if you have `.envrc` that triggers `eval $(ssh-agent -s)` in a project it can spawn agents you don't expect. Remove agent spawns from direnv and prefer a single agent in your login shell.
Micah: ah! I had `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` in a repo `.envrc` — that was creating agents per project. removing it fixed the passphrase prompts. :relieved:
Tara: nice. one more tip — for VS Code, make sure the Remote - Containers / Devcontainer picks up your login shell init. Add this to `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` if you're using code:

```
"remoteEnv": {
  "PATH": "/opt/homebrew/bin:${containerEnv:PATH}"
}
```

Micah: excellent. last snag: direnv complains about `allow` for `.envrc` after I changed files. Is that normal?
Devon: yes — run `direnv allow` in the repo after edits. It refuses to eval changed files until you explicitly allow.
Micah: everything green now — rust + node via asdf, PATH fixed, SSH keys in keychain, direnv allowed. thanks all! :tada:
Onboarding Bot: Hey Micah — congrats on finishing first-week bootstrap! You might find these docs helpful: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup and https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-templates. Ping #devex if anything else crops up.
Micah: will do, appreciate the help :raised_hands:
